nodes.label: Part A1 - This guide (reading order and identifiers)
nodes.rationale: Read first: the package is split so AMPM needs no technical background for Part A, with Part B kept as developer reference.

nodes.label: Part A2 - Decision brief
nodes.rationale: The short version carrying AMPM's answers under every question plus the eleven points still to confirm; AMPM's job here is to confirm those eleven.

nodes.label: Part A3 - Your brief, annotated
nodes.rationale: AMPM's five source documents are reproduced in full with each finding placed at the passage it concerns, so a finding is read in its own context rather than as a list.

nodes.label: Part A4 - Your flowcharts, redrawn
nodes.rationale: Supplied and upgraded versions are shown side by side with additions in green and changes in amber so AMPM can approve the structure or mark individual boxes.

nodes.label: Part A5 - Decisions we need from you (Q1 to Q25)
nodes.rationale: The 25 questions in plain language with choices, the assumption taken in place of an answer, and an answer box; the ten Tier 1 questions are to be answered first.

nodes.label: Part A6 - Assumptions we took
nodes.rationale: Every assumption made in place of an answer, grouped by theme with a confirm column, so no default stands unseen.

nodes.label: Part A7 - The questions still open (round two, R1 to R19)
nodes.rationale: Round two after the 25 October answers: the eleven points AMPM left open plus the points raised while applying the answers, written as nineteen questions (R1 to R19), each with what AMPM's documents already say, a proposal and an answer box, so a tick suffices where AMPM agrees.

nodes.label: Part B0 - decision-log.md
nodes.rationale: Generated: AMPM's answer to every question, its effect on each assumption, and the items still to confirm.

nodes.label: Part B1 - requirements-audit.md
nodes.rationale: The audit of the brief: 9 conflicts, 44 gaps, 15 ambiguities, 8 risks, 25 decisions.

nodes.label: Part B2 - decision-register.md
nodes.rationale: Generated: every assumption indexed by the question it depends on, so answering a question shows what it unblocks.

nodes.label: Part B7 - field-matrix.md and field-matrix.csv
nodes.rationale: Generated from the data-model diagrams and field_rules.py, so field type, validation, visibility and automation stay derived from one source instead of hand-maintained.

nodes.label: Identifier family Q1 to Q25 (decisions only AMPM can make)
nodes.rationale: A single prefix for every point the design cannot settle on its own, defined in Part A2 and A5 and in requirements-audit.md section 11, so an assumption can cite the question it waits on.

nodes.label: Identifier family R1 to R19 (open after the 25 October answers)
nodes.rationale: Round-two identifiers keep the second pass of open points separate from the original Q numbering, so an answered Q with a residual gap does not get reopened under its old number; defined in Part A7.

nodes.label: Identifier family CF, GP, AM, RK (audit findings)
nodes.rationale: Conflict, gap, ambiguity and risk findings are numbered per class in requirements-audit.md sections 4 to 10 and placed in context in Part A3.

nodes.label: Assumption prefixes A, P, T, U, W, V
nodes.rationale: One letter per discipline (data model, permissions, technology, flows, screens, testing) so an assumption line shows at a glance which draft it belongs to; registered in Part A6 and in section 0 of each developer draft.

nodes.label: Screen prefixes PUB, AUTH, DM, CP, TW, GR
nodes.rationale: Screens are numbered by surface (public site, sign-in, demo, client portal, team workspace, guest RSVP portal), matching the four experiences that share the system.

nodes.label: Test identifiers AC-nn.m
nodes.rationale: Each test is numbered under the acceptance criterion it proves, so a criterion's coverage is readable from the identifier.

nodes.label: Decision propagation chain (answer to assumption to tables to generated files)
nodes.source_location: How the identifiers work, closing paragraph
nodes.rationale: When AMPM answers a question the assumption lines citing it are confirmed or replaced, then the tables, screens and tests citing those lines, then the generated files are rebuilt. The citation chain exists so a single answer can be traced to everything it changes instead of requiring a document-wide re-read.

nodes.label: Generated files and their generators
nodes.rationale: field-matrix, decision-register, assumptions-taken and decision-log are rebuilt by field_matrix_build.py, decision_register_build.py, assumptions_sheet_build.py and apply_decisions.py plus decision_log_build.py from decisions.json and the assumption registers; they must never be edited by hand, because a hand edit would be lost on the next rebuild and would break the citation chain.

nodes.label: Shared page build (site_build.mjs and the private artifact)
nodes.rationale: site/index.html renders the whole package as one shareable page and --brief renders the decision brief alone; the published copy is a private claude.ai artifact that is republished after each rebuild so AMPM's link never changes.

nodes.label: Milestone schedule and cost estimate (not yet drafted)
nodes.rationale: Held deliberately until the web-portal (R4), capacity (R14) and launch-shape (R17) questions are answered, because each of those changes the amount of front-end work, the sizing and the number of releases to cost.

nodes.label: Two private repositories under the app-ampm account
nodes.rationale: ampm-platform holds the package, the audit, the source documents and the generators; ampm-vault holds the Obsidian vault. Each carries its own git identity and the git-credential-ampm.sh helper, and both scripts refuse to commit without one, so nothing is ever recorded under another GitHub account.

nodes.label: Obsidian vault (vault/)
nodes.rationale: The human-readable record: one note per question, assumption, finding and open item, session journals, D-nnn build decisions and a Bases dashboard. docs/ and reference_docs/ are synced copies that the next sync overwrites, so documents are edited in the project, never in the vault.

nodes.label: Automatic checkpoint, vault sync and journal hooks
nodes.rationale: SessionStart, Stop, post-commit and a ten-minute launchd agent commit the project, sync the vault, keep the session journal and file docs into the memory wing, so no step depends on a human remembering it; the hooks log to ~/Library/Logs.

nodes.label: MemPalace wing ampm
nodes.source_location: Session memory and the knowledge graph
nodes.rationale: Holds the transcript of every session run in this folder or its worktrees plus the design docs, as verbatim text with semantic search and no API calls; the palace itself stays local and is not committed.

nodes.label: graphify knowledge graph (graphify-out/)
nodes.source_location: Session memory and the knowledge graph
nodes.rationale: A graph of the design package, generators and source documents with each edge tagged extracted or inferred; graphify-out/ is committed so every checkout and worktree queries the same graph without rebuilding, and a PreToolUse hook points sessions at it instead of grepping.

nodes.label: wing_api collision with MemPalace's own shell hooks
nodes.source_location: Session memory and the knowledge graph, caveat paragraph
nodes.rationale: MemPalace's repository shell hooks file a running session under the shared wing wing_api without naming the project, and because drawers are keyed by content and upserted they overwrite what the project hooks wrote. Fix: point those hooks at the project-aware runner and re-key the shared wing with wings split, then rebuild hallways; done on the development Mac on 26 October 2026, and setup_memory.sh reprints the reminder.

nodes.label: Recording a confirmation from AMPM
nodes.rationale: Open-item and log notes are written once and kept, so a confirmation is recorded in the open item's note (status: confirmed) and in decisions.json, then every generator and the two shared pages are rebuilt and republished; the next checkpoint commits it and the vault follows.

nodes.label: AMPM source documents (BIZ, WHY, SPEC, TEAM-FLOW, PORTAL-FLOW)
nodes.rationale: The supplied brief lives in reference_docs/ (business explanation, Why AMPM App note, Developer Technical Specification v1.0, two Level-1 flowcharts) and the drafts cite it by these short codes; AMPM's answers of 25 October 2026 are in reference_docs/answers/.

nodes.label: MemPalace 3.11

nodes.label: Stop hook
nodes.rationale: In .claude/settings.json: runs checkpoint.sh --hook and memory_hook.sh at the end of every Claude Code turn.

nodes.label: MemPalace shared wing wing_api
nodes.rationale: The unnamed shared wing MemPalace's own global shell hooks file running transcripts under.

nodes.label: MemPalace global shell hooks caveat
nodes.rationale: MemPalace's own shell hooks (mempal_save_hook.sh, mempal_precompact_hook.sh in ~/.claude/settings.json) file a running session's transcript under the shared wing wing_api without naming the project; because MemPalace keys drawers by content and upserts, they overwrite the wing the project hooks set. Fix: point them at the project-aware runner (mempalace hook run --hook stop --harness claude-code, and --hook precompact) and re-key the shared wing with mempalace wings split --wing wing_api (plan, then --yes, then mempalace hallways --rebuild). Done on the development Mac on 26 October 2026.
